On-Chain Operator. Lesson 6.6, Vote-escrow tokenomics, bribes and governance markets. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You can already see a bridge, an oracle, and an admin key. Research starts there. A rate comes after the mechanism.
Vote-escrow: you lock a governance token for a period (often up to 4 years) and get ve-tokens with voting power that decays as the unlock approaches.
Gauges: ve-holders vote on which pools receive the protocol's token emissions.
Bribes / voting incentives: protocols that want liquidity pay ve-holders to vote for their pool.
Voters earn this as yield (plus a share of fees in some designs).
Liquid lockers / meta-governance: protocols that lock on your behalf and give you a tradable token.
It's liquid, but it can trade at a discount, and it adds a layer of risk.
Risks: long locks (you can't sell), the token's price over the lock, emissions diluting holders, and governance capture.
Work the example on paper. $10,000 of a ve-token earning ~15% APR in bribes ≈ $1,500/yr, paid in various tokens. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Check yourself. 1. What do ve-holders vote on? The answer: Which pools receive emissions (gauge weights) and other governance decisions.
Check yourself. 2. Why do protocols pay bribes? The answer: Votes direct emissions to their pools, attracting liquidity.
Check yourself. 3. Main cost of a 4-year lock? The answer: You can't sell during the lock, whatever the token's price does.
